title: A budget tracker
description:
Build the application from lesson 6.05: a budget tracker that reads commands, one per line, until `quit` or the end of the input. Split it into files: `Program.cs` (the command loop), `Ledger.cs` (the domain), `Reports.cs` and `Storage.cs`.

```
add 2026-03-01 2500 salary March pay
add 2026-03-02 -100 rent Storage unit
add 2026-03-03 -12.50 food Lunch with Ada
add 2026-03-09 -199.90 food Groceries
budget food 200
report 2026-03
quit
```

prints

```
Added #1: 2026-03-01 salary 2500.00 March pay
Added #2: 2026-03-02 rent -100.00 Storage unit
Added #3: 2026-03-03 food -12.50 Lunch with Ada
Added #4: 2026-03-09 food -199.90 Groceries
Budget for food: 200.00
Report for 2026-03
Income:     2500.00
Expenses:    312.40
Net:        2187.60
By category:
  food        212.40 of 200.00 OVER
  rent        100.00
Bye.
```

**Commands** (the command word ignores case; blank lines are ignored; amounts use `.` and are printed with 2 decimals):

| Command | Does | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `add <date> <amount> <category> <description>` | Adds a transaction; positive amounts are income, negative are expenses. The category is stored in lower case; the description is the rest of the line, words joined by single spaces. Prints `Added #<id>: <date> <category> <amount> <description>`. Ids count from 1. | Fewer than 4 arguments: `Usage: add <date> <amount> <category> <description>`. A date not in `yyyy-MM-dd` form or not a real date: `Bad date: <text>`. An amount that is not a number, is 0, or has more than 2 decimals: `Bad amount: <text>`. |
| `budget <category> <amount>` | Sets a monthly budget: `Budget for <category>: <amount>` | Not exactly 2 arguments: `Usage: budget <category> <amount>`. Amount not above 0: `Bad amount: <text>` |
| `list` or `list <yyyy-MM>` | Every transaction (or those in that month), by date then id, as `#<id> <date> <category padded to 10> <amount right-aligned in 9>  <description>`; or `No transactions.` | `Bad month: <text>` |
| `report <yyyy-MM>` | `Report for <month>`, then `Income:`, `Expenses:` and `Net:` lines (label left in 9 characters, amount right in 10; expenses shown positive), then, if there are expenses, `By category:` and a line per category: two spaces, the category in 10, the amount spent right in 8, then ` of <budget>` if it has one and ` OVER` if the spending is above it. Categories by spending (most first), then name. A month with no transactions prints `No transactions.` after the title. | `Usage: report <month>`, `Bad month: <text>` |
| `undo` | Removes the most recently added transaction still present: `Removed #<id>`, or `Nothing to undo.` | |
| `save <file>` | Writes everything as JSON: `Saved <n> transactions to <file>` | `Usage: save <file>` |
| `load <file>` | Replaces everything with the file's contents: `Loaded <n> transactions from <file>`. New ids continue after the highest loaded id; undo starts empty. | `Usage: load <file>`; a missing or invalid file: `Could not load <file>` (nothing changes) |
| `quit` | Stops. `Bye.` is printed when the program ends, whether by `quit` or the end of the input. | Anything else: `Unknown command: <word>` |
hints: Write `Ledger` first and keep it small: adding, undoing and budgets. Then the report as a function from a ledger and a month to a record, then the command loop that only parses and prints.
A `Stack<int>` of added ids makes `undo` simple: pop ids until one is still in the list (after a `load`, start with an empty stack).

`decimal.TryParse(text, NumberStyles.AllowLeadingSign | NumberStyles.AllowDecimalPoint, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var amount)` reads `-12.50`; `amount == Math.Round(amount, 2)` checks there are at most 2 decimals.

`DateOnly.TryParseExact(text, "yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out var date)` accepts only that exact form, and only real dates (it refuses `2026-02-30`). For a month such as `2026-03`, add `"-01"` and parse it the same way. `DateTimeStyles` is in `System.Globalization`.
requirements: `Ledger` (domain) knows nothing about the console or files; `Reports` builds the report with LINQ from a ledger; `Storage` saves and loads JSON with a `version` field.
Money is `decimal` throughout, formatted with the invariant culture.
The command loop turns every user mistake into a message; it never crashes on bad input.
stretch: Add `import <file.csv>` to read transactions from a bank's CSV export, using the CSV parser from practice 5.03.
